ritual.info.body1: Naming an emotion demonstrably calms the nervous system — studies show that just putting a feeling into words measurably dampens the brain's stress response.
ritual.info.body2: So the daily ritual isn't about experiencing something special every day, but about looking in briefly and regularly — small shifts show up earlier that way, before they pile up.
ritual.info.disclaimer: This does not replace therapy or diagnostics. For lasting distress, professional support is part of the picture.

beruehren.locked.body: Exercises are part of Lomira Plus — start your free 7-day trial to unlock them.
beruehren.info.body1: Touch is one of the oldest signals of safety our nervous system knows — the body responded to it even before we could speak. Rhythmic tapping or gentle pressure can put that effect to deliberate use.
beruehren.info.body2: Tapping exercises come directly from the book and are studied in the context of stress and anxiety. Acupressure points come from traditional Chinese medicine — the evidence base there is thinner; they may have a calming effect without us making any efficacy claim.
beruehren.info.disclaimer: In cases of severe trauma or acute mental illness, these exercises do not replace treatment. Professional support belongs in professional hands.
beruehren.subtitle: Gentle touch as a signal of safety. Short exercises, no processing.
exercise.eft.name: EFT basic sequence
exercise.eft.subtitle: 8 points, tap rhythmically
exercise.eft.instruction: Tap each point 5–7 times lightly with two fingertips, then move on to the next. Two rounds.
exercise.bilateral.name: Bilateral tapping
exercise.bilateral.subtitle: 2 points, alternating
exercise.bilateral.instruction: Gently tap left and right shoulder alternately. Rhythmically, eyes open or closed.
exercise.yintang.name: Yintang
exercise.yintang.subtitle: 1 point, gentle pressure
exercise.yintang.instruction: Hold gentle pressure with a fingertip between the eyebrows. Keep breathing calmly.
exercise.butterfly.name: Butterfly Hug
exercise.butterfly.subtitle: 2 points, alternating
exercise.butterfly.instruction: Hands crossed on the chest, tap alternately and gently.
exercise.hand.name: Hand points
exercise.hand.subtitle: Shenmen & Laogong
exercise.hand.instruction: Alternately press or gently rub the centre of the palm and the wrist.
exercise.ear.name: Ear Shenmen
exercise.ear.subtitle: 1 point, gentle pressure
exercise.ear.instruction: Hold gentle pressure on the upper part of the outer ear, or knead slowly.
exercise.anmian.name: Anmian
exercise.anmian.subtitle: 1 point, gentle pressure
exercise.anmian.instruction: Hold gentle pressure in the hollow behind the earlobe, or slowly circle.
exercise.neiguan.name: Neiguan
exercise.neiguan.subtitle: 1 point, gentle pressure
exercise.neiguan.instruction: Hold gentle pressure two to three finger-widths above the wrist crease, centred between the tendons.
lektionen.title: Lessons
lektionen.info.body: These lessons build directly on the book 'Warum dein Nervensystem dich zurückhält' — presented as short, self-contained units for everyday life.
lektionen.info.disclaimer: They convey knowledge about your nervous system but do not replace a diagnosis or treatment. For persistent distress, professional support is part of the picture.
